summary: Prempeh I International Airport serves Kumasi, Ghana's second-largest city and the cultural heart of the Ashanti Region. Named after Prempeh I, the 13th Asantehene (King of the Ashanti), the airport acts as a key gateway to central Ghana and supports both domestic flights and limited regional international connections. The facility has undergone modernization efforts to expand capacity and improve passenger services.
faqs:
Q: How far is Prempeh I International Airport from Kumasi city center?
A: The airport is located approximately 10 kilometers northwest of central Kumasi, typically a 20 to 30 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Which airlines operate from Prempeh I International Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves domestic carriers including Africa World Airlines and PassionAir, with flights connecting Kumasi to Accra and occasional regional services.

Q: Does the airport have international flights?
A: Yes, despite its focus on domestic traffic, the airport handles select regional international flights, primarily to nearby West African destinations.

Q: Are there currency exchange services available at the airport?
A: Banking and currency exchange facilities are available, though it is advisable to exchange or withdraw Ghanaian cedis in the city for better rates.
transport_tips: Taxis and ride-hailing services are the most reliable ways to reach central Kumasi, with official airport taxis available just outside the terminal. Tro-tros (shared minibuses) operate along the main road nearby but are less convenient with luggage. Pre-arranging a hotel pickup is recommended for first-time visitors, especially during evening arrivals.
local_tip: Visit the nearby Manhyia Palace Museum, the official residence of the Asantehene, which is just a short drive from the airport and offers deep insight into Ashanti history and the legacy behind the airport's name.
